findings.message: There are now two ways to compute an entity's today. `entityDay` does it in Postgres (`timestamptz at time zone <zone>`, falling back to UTC), and `entityToday` in `modules/hr/server/zones.ts:12` does it in Node with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`. Both use the same zone rule (`entityZoneSql`), but the date arithmetic runs on two different tz databases: Postgres's and Node's ICU. `change_person` picks the period's start with `entityToday`, while the in-force reads (`employmentAt`, `getEmployment`, `personByNo`) pick the period with `entityDay`. Fix: have `entityToday` check the zone, then return `select to_char(${entityDay(sql`${entityId}::uuid`)}, 'YYYY-MM-DD')`, so one function computes the date.
findings.scenario: Postgres and Node ship different tzdata for a zone whose offset rule changed, and a department change happens near local midnight. change_person writes the period starting on the JS date, while get_person reads on the SQL date, which is a day earlier. The change the person just confirmed doesn't appear until the next day.

findings.message: `export { entityToday, noZone };` re-exports the helpers that moved to `zones.ts`, but nothing imports them from `services.ts`. `change.ts` imports from `./zones`, and no test or UI file imports `entityToday` or `noZone` from services. Delete the re-export.

The diff changes the contract reads' default date (`getPerson`, `listPeople`, `getEmployment`, `reportUserIds`) from UTC today to each person's entity's own today, falling back to UTC for an unzoned entity. It also adds the `get_legal_entity` read tool and makes the `hr.person.status` job fail, naming the unzoned entities. The README still says the as-of date defaults to 'today', and its Jobs line doesn't mention the new failure. contracts.ts's header comment was updated, but the README wasn't. Update both README lines.

This test drafts and confirms allocations for 2027-03 through 2028-01 against the real clock; it never fakes the date. The repo already has date drift breaking CI, for example the allocations e2e that expires on 2027-02-01. Once the real date passes these months, allocate may refuse or change the draft and the test will break. Fake the date with `vi.setSystemTime`, or compute the months relative to now.
findings.scenario: Run in April 2027: 2027-03 is now in the past, so the drafted card or the confirm changes and `action.look.done` no longer equals 'Added Dinesh Wickrama to CON · 40% Mar–May'.
